lesson_title: Grouping in Pairs: The Minus That Must Come Out
hook_text: One minus sign jams the whole method. Here's how to set it free.
clip_script: Now the second pair — and here is the trap. Minus n p minus n q clearly shares n. Try positive n first: the bracket comes out as minus p minus q. The first pair produced p plus q. They do not match, and without a shared bracket the third move cannot happen. The method stalls. Now try negative n. Dividing minus n p by minus n leaves positive p, because a minus divided by a minus turns positive. Every sign inside the bracket flipped, and the bracket now reads p plus q — a perfect twin. Here is the rule: when a pair begins with a minus sign, factor out a negative common factor.
visual_style: Two grocery bags on a counter: the first opens to a glowing (p + q), the second jams shut with mirrored red brackets until a minus sign is lifted out and both bags click open in matching green.
mood: Puzzle-box tension resolving into a satisfying click.
pacing: Slow build on the jammed bag, sharp release at the flip, brisk clean finish.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and lift out the shared bracket yourself.
